text:
leah: Quick heads up — planning a change to edge auth validation tomorrow morning. Proxy will prefer service-account tokens (aud="svc") for project routing/attribution, and only fall back to org API keys if SA token is missing. Need a short canary + telemetry checklist.

ashok: +1 for preferring SA tokens. Main risk is customers using legacy org keys expecting project-level quotas. We should emit an explicit metric when fallback is used: `auth.fallback_used` with labels `org`, `project` (maybe `unknown`).

sam: Console/UX question: how will keys surface? We should add a visible `scope` column in the Keys list (Org vs Project vs SA) and show a tooltip: "If SA token present, it wins routing." Helps support.

nora: Telemetry thoughts: publish counts for `auth.method` = {"sa","org_key","client_cert"}, and `routing.result` = {"routed_project","routed_org","rejected"}. Also capture `quota.attributed_to` tag. We can add an alert if `routed_project == unknown` spikes.

leah: Good. For canary: start with 1% of edge traffic in us-west for 4 hours, then 10% for 2 hours if no increase in `auth.rejection_rate` or `billing.attribution_mismatch` (>0.1%). Feature flag `edge.auth.prefer_sa` to gate behavior.

kevin: Suggest adding a debug header for canary to trace routing: `X-RW-Auth-Method: sa|org_key`, and `X-RW-Routed-To: project/<id>` so logs show both. Example proxy snippet:

```
# envoy lua snippet (concept)
function on_request(request)
  local jwt = request:headers()["Authorization"]
  if jwt and claims(jwt).aud == "svc" then
    request:headers()["X-RW-Auth-Method"] = "sa"
    route_by_claims(claims(jwt))
  else
    request:headers()["X-RW-Auth-Method"] = "org_key"
    route_by_org_header(request:headers()["x-rw-org-key"]) 
  end
end
```

ashok: Nice. Also add a short log line format to search across stacks: `auth=sa|org_key routed_to=project:<id>|org:<id> fallback_used=true|false` so we can run quick SLO checks.

sam: Migration script idea: backfill `service_account_id` into requests table for the last 30 days where we can infer it from JWTs, then run a comparison: `count(routed_project != inferred_project)` to estimate impact. Query example (psuedo):

```
SELECT count(*) FROM requests
WHERE inferred_sa IS NOT NULL AND routed_project != inferred_sa_project
```

nora: For dashboard: add a small panel in Console -> Observability -> Auth that shows breakdown by `auth.method` and a heatmap for `fallback_used` by org. Also expose a link to sample requests (click to open logs).

leah: Rollout playbook:
- Create FF `edge.auth.prefer_sa` default=false
- Deploy proxy change behind FF to all regions (no traffic switch)
- Enable FF in canary region/1% for 4h 
- Monitor `auth.rejection_rate`, `auth.method`, `routed_project` mismatch; run support smoke test playbook
- If OK -> 10% for 2h -> full.

kevin: Who owns the support smoke tests? I'd volunteer infra-oncall to run a small checklist: create SA token, call endpoint, verify header + project attribution, create org key fallback case, verify fallback metric.

leah: @kevin thanks. Action items:
1) ashok add fallback metric + log line (PR to router)
2) nora add telemetry & dashboard panels (Grafana + Console card)
3) sam/ux add `scope` column to Keys page + tooltip
4) kevin owner for smoke test runbook + headers for tracing
5) leah will open FF and coordinate canary window

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: edge-router v3.14.2 -> canary cluster us-west-2 at 2026-03-21T09:00Z (FF off).

sam: Small note — add migration warning in Console when a customer creates a new org key: "SA tokens preferred for project attribution; consider creating a service account." Link to docs.

ashok: One more: ensure rate-limiter uses `attributed_project` from the same routing decision. We don't want to double-count if fallback flips after rate-limit check. Order of operations: auth -> routing -> rate-limit -> serve. Document in PR.

leah: Perfect. I'll draft the RFC/PR and tag folks. If anyone wants to review the proxy snippet I'll drop a branch in infra-edge. :eyes: 

kevin: I'll add tests for header emission and small end-to-end canary checklist.

nora: I'll stub the dashboard and add initial panels to staging Grafana.

leah: Thanks all — aiming to start canary tomorrow.
